chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father from Ali (peace be upon him)

That he complained of his eye, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) visited him, and behold, Ali (peace be upon him) was crying out. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Is it grief or pain, O Ali?' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have never had pain greater than it.'
He said, 'O Ali, indeed when the Angel of Death descends to take the soul of the disbeliever, he descends with him with a skewer of fire, and he pulls out his soul with it, so Hell cries out.'
So Ali (peace be upon him) sat up and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, repeat your statement to me, for my pain has made me forget what you said. Does this happen to anyone from your ummah?'
He said, 'Yes, unjust rulers, and those who consume the property of the orphan, and the witness of false testimony.'
ai.seo_question: Who else experiences the same pain as a disbeliever at the hands of the Angel of Death?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on judges, this hadith establishes a profound spiritual parallel between the physical agony of the dying and the cosmic distress of Hell. The Prophet’s confirmation that unjust rulers (*hukkam jairin*), devourers of orphans' wealth, and false witnesses share this fate underscores the severity of their sins in Shia jurisprudence, linking their moral corruption directly to the mechanics of the afterlife.
